title: A closure token marks an exhaustive list rather than another list item
summary: A list-closure hypothesis assigns a special terminal form the function of declaring that all members of a bounded category have been listed.

design.unit: enumerated records with a final member and a candidate terminal closure form
design.prediction: When the closure form appears, no independently identified category member is omitted; open lists may omit members but cannot use the closure form in the same slot.
design.countermodel: The same surface pattern could arise from a context-conditioned lexical convention or editorial packaging without the proposed semantic mechanism.
design.falsifier: A closure-bearing record has a documented omitted member, or an open list uses the same terminal form in the licensed closure slot.
design.principal_risk: Category membership and completeness require independent annotation; this is not a claim that current lists are exhaustive. Adjacent to quantity designs but predicts omission/completeness, not amount.
